definition_en: a child's word for father; an informal or affectionate name for one's father
core_image: 小孩伸手要抱的那个人：家里最让孩子安心的大个子
scene: 小女孩在游乐场摔倒了，眼泪汪汪地张开双臂跑向栏杆外。"Daddy, pick me up!" she cried, running toward the fence.
sceneCN: 这里 daddy 是「爸爸、爹地」（第 1 个义项：孩子对父亲的亲昵称呼）；句意是小女孩哭着喊爸爸来抱她。

pos.zh: 爸爸；爹地（儿语、亲昵称呼）

collocations.zh: 爸爸的小棉袄；最受宠的女儿

derivatives.zh: 由儿语叠词截短而来，义为「爸爸」，比 daddy 稍正式
标准称呼「父亲」，与儿语 daddy 相对
由 daddy 加形容词后缀 -ish 构成，义为「爸爸似的」

senses.title: A child's affectionate word for father
senses.definition: the word children use to talk to or about their father
senses.definitionCN: 孩子用来称呼自己父亲的词，语气亲昵
senses.example: Daddy will read you a story tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚爸爸会给你读一个故事。
senses.why: The doubled syllable -dy is baby talk, softening the adult word into something small and safe.
senses.whyCN: 叠音 -dy 是典型的儿语构形，把成人的「父亲」软化成孩子口中的亲昵称呼。

senses.title: An informal affectionate address to any older man or figure
senses.definition: informal use for a protective or beloved male figure, sometimes playfully
senses.definitionCN: 口语中对有保护意味或深受爱戴的男性角色的昵称，常带玩笑色彩
senses.example: Thanks for fixing my laptop, daddy!
senses.exampleCN: 谢谢你帮我修电脑，老爸！
senses.why: The protective image of a father extends playfully to anyone who takes care of you.
senses.whyCN: 「父亲是保护者」的画面被扩展到任何照顾你的人身上，成为一种玩笑式的亲昵。

senses.title: A dominant or authoritative male figure
senses.definition: informal slang for a man who is the biggest, oldest, or most dominant of his kind
senses.definitionCN: 俚语中指某一类里最大、最老资格或最具支配地位的人物
senses.example: This old truck is the daddy of all off-road vehicles.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆老卡车是所有越野车里的大佬。
senses.why: The family image of the biggest, strongest person in the house maps onto the biggest of any class.
senses.whyCN: 家里「最大最强的人」的画面映射到同类事物中「最大的那个」，成为俚语用法。

intro.en: Daddy belongs to the family of nursery words for parents, formed by doubling a simple syllable.
intro.cn: daddy 属于儿语里称呼父母的词族，通过叠用简单音节构成。

items.en: Generally traced to the earliest syllables infants produce, such as *da or similar velar/bilabial babble; a reconstructed form that arose independently in nearly all languages.
items.cn: 一般认为来自婴幼儿最早发出的音节 *da 一类的声音，重构形式，世界语言中普遍独立产生。

items.en: Old English used fæder as the standard word for father; the baby-talk form dad existed alongside it from an early period.
items.cn: 古英语的标准词是 fæder「父亲」，儿语形式的 dad 很早便与之并行存在。

items.en: The diminutive form daddy, with the affectionate suffix -y, is first recorded around the early 16th century.
items.cn: 带亲昵后缀 -y 的 daddy 约在十六世纪初首次见于记录。

items.en: The word spread through family speech and children's literature, staying firmly informal.
items.cn: 该词通过家庭用语和儿童文学传播，始终保持口语色彩。

items.en: Modern usage keeps daddy as a child's word, while slang extends it to dominant figures and machines.
items.cn: 现代用法中 daddy 主要是孩子的称呼，俚语里还扩展出「大佬、主导者」的用法。

note.en: Daddy is easy to confuse with its plain parent word dad and with father, and with look-alike words in other languages.
note.cn: daddy 容易与它的基础词 dad、标准词 father 混淆，也要注意与其他语言里拼写相近的词区分。

entries.definition: informal word for father, less childish than daddy
entries.definitionCN: 「爸爸」，同样口语，但不如 daddy 幼儿化，是 daddy 截短的基础词

entries.definition: the standard, formal word for a male parent
entries.definitionCN: 「父亲」的标准正式说法；与儿语 daddy 同指一人但语域完全不同

entries.definition: a crane fly or harvestman with very long thin legs
entries.definitionCN: 「盲蛛；大蚊」，一种长着细长腿的昆虫；与 daddy 共用开头但指虫不指人

entries.definition: another affectionate child's word for father, from French
entries.definitionCN: 「爸爸」的另一种儿语说法，源自法语，语感比 daddy 略旧

entries.definition: a short informal form for father, rural or old-fashioned
entries.definitionCN: 「爸」的极简口语形式，带乡村或旧式色彩

entries.definition: informal American word for father
entries.definitionCN: 美式口语「老爸」，与 daddy 同为亲昵非正式称呼

normalIntro.en: Build daddy from its family and sound shape.
normalIntro.cn: 用词族和声音形态记住 daddy。

normal.en: dad + -y: the affectionate suffix turns dad into the childish daddy.
normal.cn: dad 加亲昵后缀 -y，就成了更幼儿化的 daddy。

normal.en: The double d mirrors other nursery words: mommy, doggy, kitty.
normal.cn: 双写 d 与 mommy、doggy、kitty 一样，是典型儿语叠音。

normal.en: Plural daddies keeps the baby-talk pattern of ladies, puppies.
normal.cn: 复数 daddies 的变音和 ladies、puppies 一致，符合儿语规律。

normal.en: Compare family: dad, daddy, father — from casual to formal.
normal.cn: 词族排序：dad、daddy、father，从随意到正式。

normal.en: Sound cue: /ˈdæ/ repeats twice, easy for a toddler to say.
normal.cn: 读音 /ˈdædi/ 的音节重复，正是幼儿最容易发出的音。

abstract.en: Picture small arms reaching up toward a tall figure at the door.
abstract.cn: 想象门口那个高大的身影，小手臂高高举起要抱抱。

abstract.en: Feel the soft double thump of two d's, like a child patting twice.
abstract.cn: 感受两个 d 的柔软双重音，像孩子拍两下手。

abstract.en: Hear a bedtime voice saying the word slowly and warmly.
abstract.cn: 耳边响起睡前温柔缓慢喊出的那个称呼。

examples.en: Daddy promised to take us to the beach on Sunday.
examples.cn: 爸爸答应周日带我们去海边。

examples.en: The little girl drew a picture of mommy and daddy holding hands.
examples.cn: 小女孩画了一幅妈妈和爸爸手牵手的画。

examples.en: Among collectors, this rare stamp is the daddy of them all.
examples.cn: 在收藏家眼里，这枚珍稀邮票是所有邮票中的老大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爹地」——发音几乎就是中文的「爹地」，孩子奶声奶气喊的那声「爹地」就是 daddy，无需另造联想。

root: 儿语叠词：dad（儿语「爸爸」，一般认为源自幼儿最早发出的音节，属重构形式）+ 亲昵后缀 -y；与 fæder（古英语「父亲」）并行而非其派生，标准词 father 另有日耳曼语源。

sensesIntro.en: From the nursery address to father, the word stretches playfully to any protector and then to the biggest of a kind.
sensesIntro.cn: 从孩子对父亲的称呼出发，玩笑式地扩展到任何保护者，再引申为同类中的「最大者、大佬」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the small child's word for the tall protector of the house
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子口中对家中高大保护者的称呼

branches.en: the nursery word itself
branches.cn: 儿语称呼本身

branches.en: affection extends beyond the family
branches.cn: 亲昵称呼溢出家庭范围

branches.en: playful address to a helper or protector
branches.cn: 对帮助者、保护者的玩笑称呼

branches.en: the biggest and oldest of a class
branches.cn: 同类中最大最老资格者

branches.en: slang for dominance in machines or things
branches.cn: 俚语中指机器、事物的「老大」

intro.en: Daddy is built from a nursery base plus the affectionate suffix -y; its family shows how English makes diminutives.
intro.cn: daddy 由儿语词基加亲昵后缀 -y 构成；它的词族展示了英语如何构造小称形式。

latinIntro.en: Daddy has no Latin ancestry; the -y suffix descends from Old English rather than Latin, so no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: daddy 没有拉丁语来源；后缀 -y 出自古英语而非拉丁语，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.meaningCN: 儿语「爸爸」，daddy 的基础词
亲昵小称后缀，表示「小、可爱、幼儿化」
items.exampleCN: 小狗、小猫、宝宝，同用 -y 后缀

items.meaningCN: 与 daddy 平行的「妈妈」儿语形式

items.example: The daddies watched the school play.
items.exampleCN: 爸爸们观看学校的演出。

items.meaningCN: 「盲蛛；大蚊」复合词，借 daddy 的口语色彩
items.example: A daddy longlegs sat on the windowsill.

items.meaningCN: 与儿语相对的标准词「父亲」，来源不同
爸爸似的、有父亲做派的
源自法语的同类儿语词

definition_en: silly or foolish; (British, informal) crazy or senseless
core_image: 拍脑门的傻气：明摆着的事偏要做反
scene: 他把伞留在家，冒着瓢泼大雨走了整条街。"Don't be daft—take my umbrella!" his neighbour shouted.
sceneCN: 这里 daft 是「傻的、愚蠢的」（第 1 个义项：做事不明智的傻气）；句意是邻居骂他傻，让他拿伞。

pos.zh: 愚蠢的；傻的；（英式口语）疯疯癫癫的

derivatives.zh: 由 daft 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「傻乎乎地」
由 daft 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「愚蠢；傻气」

senses.title: Foolish or silly in behaviour
senses.definition: acting in a silly way that shows poor judgement
senses.definitionCN: 行事傻气、判断力差的
senses.example: It was daft to leave the windows open in a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨天开着窗户真傻。
senses.why: The original sense was gentle or meek; English shifted it to harmless silliness.
senses.whyCN: 该词原义是「温顺」，英语里逐渐偏移为无害的傻气、不明智。

senses.title: Crazy or insane (British informal)
senses.definition: behaving as if out of one's mind; slightly mad
senses.definitionCN: 举止像失去理智似的，有点疯
senses.example: The noise from the construction site is driving me daft.
senses.exampleCN: 工地的噪音快把我逼疯了。
senses.why: Silliness pushed one step further becomes madness; the mild word can climb to the strong sense.
senses.whyCN: 傻气再往前一步就是疯癫，温和的词被推向了强烈的用法。

senses.title: Foolish in a playful, affectionate way
senses.definition: used teasingly about someone you like, without real criticism
senses.definitionCN: 带调侃地形容喜欢的人，并非真的批评
senses.example: You daft old fool, you forgot your own birthday!
senses.exampleCN: 你这个傻老头，把自己的生日都忘了！
senses.why: Because the word stays informal and mild, it works as teasing rather than insult.
senses.whyCN: 因为词感口语而温和，它常被用作玩笑式打趣而非辱骂。

intro.en: Daft began as a word for gentle or meek and slid, over centuries, into foolish and then crazy.
intro.cn: daft 最初表示「温顺、文雅」，历经数百年滑向「愚蠢」，再到「疯癫」。

items.en: Old English gedefe meant gentle, fitting, or meek; the shortened form def(e) survived in Middle English.
items.cn: 古英语 gedefe 意为「温顺、合适」，其截短形式 def(e) 在中古英语中仍在使用。

items.en: Middle English daft first meant gentle or mild, then came to mean foolish or stupid.
items.cn: 中古英语 daft 先表「温和」，随后转为「愚蠢、迟钝」。

items.en: By the 16th–17th centuries the word covered silly behaviour and mild insanity; Shakespeare used it in both flavours.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪，该词已兼指傻气与轻度疯癫；莎士比亚两种用法都用过。

items.en: In Scottish and Northern English the older senses survived longer, including 'meek' in Scots law contexts.
items.cn: 在苏格兰和英格兰北部方言中，旧义「温顺」保留更久，苏格兰法律用语里仍在使用。

items.en: Today daft is chiefly British informal for silly, with daft as a brush among the best-known idioms.
items.cn: 如今 daft 主要作英式口语「傻的」，习语 daft as a brush 最为著名。

note.en: Watch the spelling daft against draft and raft, and compare its meaning with other silly-words.
note.cn: 注意 daft 与 draft、raft 的拼写区分，并与其它表「傻」的词比较用法。

entries.definition: a preliminary version of a document, or a current of air
entries.definitionCN: 「草稿；气流」，与 daft 仅差一个字母 r，词源不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: a flat floating platform of logs
entries.definitionCN: 「木筏」，与 daft 形近，词义无关

entries.definition: skilful and quick with the hands
entries.definitionCN: 「灵巧的」，与 daft 同韵且词形相近，意思却几乎相反

entries.definition: foolish in a light, often endearing way
entries.definitionCN: 「傻的」，语气轻快常带可爱意味，是 daft 最接近的通用对应词

entries.definition: showing lack of good sense
entries.definitionCN: 「愚蠢的」，比 daft 稍正式，强调判断力差

entries.definition: British informal for crazy or angry
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语「疯的；生气的」，在疯癫义上与 daft 相通

normalIntro.en: Anchor daft with its sound shape and its British partners.
normalIntro.cn: 用发音形态和英式搭档记住 daft。

normal.en: daft rhymes with draft; remember: don't draft a daft plan.
normal.cn: daft 与 draft 押韵，可记「别把傻主意写成草案」。

normal.en: Idiom: daft as a brush paints a brush that cannot think.
normal.cn: 习语 daft as a brush（傻得像把刷子）画面感极强。

normal.en: drive someone daft = drive someone mad, same pattern.
normal.cn: drive someone daft 与 drive someone mad 结构相同，可互相替换记忆。

normal.en: Derived pair: daftly (adv.) and daftness (n.) follow the regular pattern.
normal.cn: 派生对：daftly（副词）和 daftness（名词）按规则后缀构成。

normal.en: It is chiefly British: American English prefers silly or dumb.
normal.cn: 该词主要用于英式英语，美式英语更常说 silly 或 dumb。

abstract.en: Picture someone walking into the rain with the umbrella left at home.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人伞落在家里、径直走进大雨的画面。

abstract.en: Feel the flat, blunt sound /dɑːft/ like a wooden clunk on the head.
abstract.cn: 感受 /dɑːft/ 那种平直钝响，像木棍敲头的闷声。

abstract.en: Hear a friend laughing and calling you daft, not angry.
abstract.cn: 耳边是朋友笑着喊你傻，并无恶意。

examples.en: It would be daft to sell the house now, when prices are so low.
examples.cn: 现在房价这么低就卖房子，太傻了。

examples.en: The puppy kept chasing its own tail like a daft little thing.
examples.cn: 小狗一直追自己的尾巴，傻乎乎的。

examples.en: Stop that whistling—it's driving me daft!
examples.cn: 别吹口哨了——快把我逼疯了！

dict_mnemonic.text: 「打夫特」——傻到被人「打」也「特」别憨；谐音仅助记，真实词源是古英语「温顺」义的偏移。

root: 古英语 gedefe（温和的、合适的）经截短与语音演变成为中古英语 daft；原义「温顺」→「迟钝」→「愚蠢」→「疯癫」，属词义贬化，非拉丁语源。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from plain silliness, up to mild madness, and sideways into affectionate teasing.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从单纯的傻气爬升到轻度疯癫，又横向转为善意的调侃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the head-slapping silliness of doing the obvious thing wrong
core.cn: 核心意象：明摆着的事偏做反的拍脑门傻气

branches.en: silly judgement in everyday acts
branches.cn: 日常行为中的傻气判断

branches.en: a daft idea or plan
branches.cn: 愚蠢的主意或计划

branches.en: teasing someone you like
branches.cn: 对喜欢的人的调侃

branches.en: slightly mad behaviour
branches.cn: 疯疯癫癫的举止

branches.en: noise or irritation driving you daft
branches.cn: 噪音或烦扰把人逼疯

intro.en: Daft is a single Germanic adjective; its small family shows regular adjectival derivation.
intro.cn: daft 是单一的日耳曼源形容词；其小词族按规则派生。

latinIntro.en: Daft has no Latin ancestry, coming from Old English gedefe; no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: daft 源自古英语 gedefe，与拉丁语无关，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.exampleCN: 他傻乎乎地忘了带钥匙。

items.meaningCN: 近义词「傻的」，语感更通用
近义词「疯的」，英式口语中与 daft 互通

items.example: He's daft as a brush but kind.

definition_en: happening or done every day; a newspaper published every day
core_image: 太阳每天照常升起：日复一日的循环
scene: 面包店门口排起长队，烤炉的香味飘满整条街。The bakery bakes fresh bread daily for the whole neighbourhood.
sceneCN: 这里 daily 是「每天」（第 4 个义项：作副词，表示每日发生）；句意是面包店每天为整个街区烤新鲜面包。

derivatives.zh: 基础词「一天；日」，daily 由它加后缀构成
由 day 加 light 构成，义为「日光；白天」
由 day 加 time 构成，义为「白天；日间」

senses.title: Happening every day
senses.definition: occurring once a day or every day as a pattern
senses.definitionCN: 按天发生的，每天一次或天天如此的
senses.example: The daily train leaves at six in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这班日班车每天早上六点发车。
senses.why: Day plus -ly builds an adjective meaning 'of each day', straight from the base noun.
senses.whyCN: day 加 -ly 直接构出「属于每一天的」形容词，语义由基础词顺延。

senses.title: Belonging to ordinary, everyday life
senses.definition: typical of or used in ordinary daily existence
senses.definitionCN: 属于普通日常生活的、惯常使用的
senses.example: She wrote about the small daily struggles of family life.
senses.exampleCN: 她写下了家庭生活中那些细碎的日常挣扎。
senses.why: Repetition every day becomes routine, so the word stretches from frequency to ordinariness.
senses.whyCN: 天天重复就成了惯例，词义从频率延伸到「平凡、日常」。

senses.title: Computed for a single day
senses.definition: measured or paid for one day, as with wages or rates
senses.definitionCN: 以一天为单位计算或支付的，如工资、费率
senses.example: Workers demanded an increase in their daily wage.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求提高日薪。
senses.why: The span of one day becomes the unit for measuring money or output.
senses.whyCN: 「一天」这个时间段被用作计量单位，于是有了按日计酬、按日计费。

senses.title: Every day (adverb)
senses.definition: once each day; on every day
senses.definitionCN: 每天一次；每一天都
senses.example: He jogs in the park daily before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早饭前在公园跑步。
senses.why: The adjective converts to an adverb to say how often something happens.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作副词，用来回答「多久一次」的问题。

senses.title: A newspaper published every day
senses.definition: a newspaper printed and sold every day
senses.definitionCN: 每天印刷发行的报纸
senses.example: She reads the local daily with her morning coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 她边喝早咖啡边读当地的日报。
senses.why: The publishing schedule of every day names the product itself.
senses.whyCN: 「每天出版」的节奏直接命名了产品本身，频率词转指出版物。

intro.en: Daily is an English formation on the Germanic word day, with no Latin passage.
intro.cn: daily 是在日耳曼基础词 day 上构成的英语本土词，不经拉丁语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *dagaz meant day, the bright span between two nights.
items.cn: 重构词根 *dagaz 意为「白天」，即两个夜晚之间的明亮时段。

items.en: Old English dæg meant day; the adverbial-adjective pattern -lic (modern -ly) already formed words like dæghwamlic.
items.cn: 古英语 dæg 即「日」；后缀 -lic（现代 -ly）当时已能构出「每天的」一类词。

items.en: Middle English daili appears as both adjective and adverb by the 14th–15th centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语 daili 在十四、十五世纪已兼作形容词和副词。

items.en: The noun sense 'daily newspaper' emerges in the 17th century as regular news printing begins.
items.cn: 十七世纪定期新闻印刷兴起，「日报」的名词义随之出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps all three uses: adjective, adverb, and the newspaper noun.
items.cn: 现代英语保留三种用法：形容词、副词与日报名词。

note.en: Do not mix daily with the adverb-ly of adjectives like lovely, and keep it apart from diary.
note.cn: 不要把 daily 与 lovely 一类形容词的 -ly 混为一谈，也要与 diary 区分开。

entries.definition: a book in which you record daily events
entries.definitionCN: 「日记簿」，与 daily 拼写相近且词源相关（都来自 day），但词性词义不同

entries.definition: a place where milk is kept and milk products are made
entries.definitionCN: 「乳品场；奶制品」，与 daily 仅一字母之差，词源不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: a small white wildflower; from 'day's eye'
entries.definitionCN: 「雏菊」，词源确与 day's eye 相关，形近 daily 但指花

entries.definition: ordinary, habitual (adjective only)
entries.definitionCN: 「日常的」，仅作形容词（every day 才是副词短语），与 daily 第 2 义项相近

entries.definition: happening at fixed intervals
entries.definitionCN: 「定期的；规律的」，强调间隔固定，与每日义相邻

entries.definition: a fixed usual sequence of actions
entries.definitionCN: 「例行公事；惯例」，由每日重复凝成的固定流程

normalIntro.en: Build daily directly from day plus -ly.
normalIntro.cn: daily 直接由 day 加 -ly 记住。

normal.en: day + -ly = of each day; the formula never fails.
normal.cn: day 加 -ly 即「每天的」，公式简单可靠。

normal.en: Three roles in one word: adjective (daily walk), adverb (walk daily), noun (a daily).
normal.cn: 一词三用：形容词（daily walk）、副词（walk daily）、名词（a daily 日报）。

normal.en: Spelling twins to separate: dairy (milk), diary (journal), daisy (flower).
normal.cn: 拼写三胞胎要分清：dairy 奶制品、diary 日记、daisy 雏菊。

normal.en: Phrase on a daily basis is the formal way to say 'every day'.
normal.cn: on a daily basis 是「每天」的正式说法。

normal.en: Compare family: hourly, weekly, monthly, yearly — same -ly pattern.
normal.cn: 词族对比：hourly、weekly、monthly、yearly，同为「时间 + -ly」。

abstract.en: See the sun rise again over the same street every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳每天清晨照常升起在同一条街道上。

abstract.en: Feel the rhythm of brushing teeth: same time, every day.
abstract.cn: 感受刷牙的节律：每天同一时间，从不间断。

abstract.en: Hear the paper hitting the doorstep at dawn, day after day.
abstract.cn: 耳边响起清晨报纸落到门阶的声音，日复一日。

examples.en: Daily exercise keeps both body and mind in shape.
examples.cn: 每天锻炼让身体和头脑都保持良好状态。

examples.en: The bakery bakes fresh bread daily for the neighbourhood.
examples.cn: 面包店每天为街区烤新鲜面包。

examples.en: Most cities used to have two dailies, morning and evening.
examples.cn: 大多数城市过去都有晨报和晚报两家日报。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爹一天一次的」——联想成「爹每天来的」，一天不落；谐音仅助记，真实构词是 day 加后缀 -ly。

root: 日耳曼本土构词：day（古英语 dæg「日」，源自重构词根 *dagaz）+ 后缀 -ly（古英语 -lic「具有…性质的」）；与拉丁语无关，同族词有 weekly、monthly 等。

sensesIntro.en: Frequency first, then the ordinariness of repeated routine, the day as a unit of measure, and finally the newspaper named by its schedule.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是频率义，再是重复而成的日常义，然后「一天」成为计量单位，最后由出版节奏命名日报。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun rising on schedule, day after day
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳按日升起，日复一日的循环

branches.en: something that happens once a day
branches.cn: 每天发生一次的事

branches.en: the ordinary texture of life
branches.cn: 日常生活的平凡质感

branches.en: a day as the unit of pay or rate
branches.cn: 以天为单位的工资、费率

branches.en: answering 'how often?' with 'every day'
branches.cn: 用「每天」回答频率

branches.en: the newspaper named after its schedule
branches.cn: 以出版节奏命名的日报

intro.en: Daily shows the English time-word plus -ly pattern that also gives weekly and yearly.
intro.cn: daily 体现了「时间词 + -ly」的英语构词模式，weekly、yearly 同属此列。

latinIntro.en: Daily is purely Germanic; the -ly suffix here is Old English -lic, not the Latin adverbial -ly, so no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: daily 是纯日耳曼词；此处 -ly 出自古英语 -lic，并非拉丁来源，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.meaningCN: 基础词「一天」，daily 的构词核心
「具有…性质」的形容词后缀，此处表频率
与 daily 平行的「每小时」
「日常的」复合词，注意与 every day（每天）区分
「乳品场」，形近词，源自古英语 dǣge（揉面的人）一路演变
「日记簿」，源自拉丁 dies（日），与 daily 意义相关但拼写相近易混
「雏菊」，字面即「白昼之眼」，花瓣随日开合

definition_en: harm done to something, or to harm it
core_image: 冰雹在车顶砸出一片细小的坑
scene: 冰雹过后，车顶多了一片密密麻麻的小坑。The hail damaged every car on the street.
sceneCN: 这里 damaged 是 damage 的过去式，指「损坏」（第 2 个义项：使东西受损）；句意是冰雹砸坏了街上每一辆车。

senses.title: Harm done to a thing
senses.definition: physical harm that makes something less useful or sound
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变得不好用或不完整的实体损伤
senses.example: The storm caused damage to the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨给屋顶造成了损坏。
senses.why: A thing is damaged when it can no longer do its job.
senses.whyCN: 当一个东西干不了它的活，它就是被损坏了。

senses.title: To harm something
senses.definition: to harm something or make it worse
senses.definitionCN: 伤害某物或使其状况变差
senses.example: The hail damaged every car on the street.
senses.exampleCN: 冰雹砸坏了街上每一辆车。
senses.why: Damage is what the blow leaves behind on the surface.
senses.whyCN: 损坏，就是那一击在表面上留下的东西。

senses.title: Money paid for harm
senses.definition: money paid to repair or make up for harm, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 为修复或弥补损害而支付的钱，通常用复数
senses.example: The court ordered him to pay damages.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令他支付赔偿金。
senses.why: When a thing cannot be mended, money is asked to stand in for it.
senses.whyCN: 东西修不好时，就请钱来代替它。

intro.en: Damage comes from Latin damnum, loss or cost, through Old French damage.
intro.cn: damage 源自拉丁语 damnum（损失、代价），经古法语 damage 进入英语。

items.en: Damnum meant loss, cost, or harm.
items.cn: damnum 意为损失、代价或伤害。

items.en: Damnare meant to cause a loss or condemn.
items.cn: damnare 意为使受损失或宣判。

items.en: Damage named harm and the loss it caused.
items.cn: damage 指伤害以及它带来的损失。

items.en: Damage entered English for injury to property.
items.cn: damage 进入英语，指对财物的损伤。

items.en: The plural damages named money paid in law.
items.cn: 复数 damages 指法律上支付的赔偿金。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dam- opening, and the meaning group names other kinds of harm.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dam- 开头，近义组列出其他形式的伤害。

entries.definition: a wall that holds back water
to condemn or swear at
slightly wet
injury or damage to someone or something
harm done to a body
the fact of no longer having something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with hail on a car roof and end with a court order to pay.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从砸在车顶的冰雹开始，落到法院的赔付命令。

normal.en: Damage is the bill the world sends after a blow.
normal.cn: 损坏，是世界在打击之后寄来的账单。

normal.en: A thing is damaged when it stops doing what it was made for.
normal.cn: 东西做不了它原本该做的事，就是损坏了。

normal.en: Reputation can be damaged without a single broken object.
normal.cn: 名声可以被损害，却一件东西都没碎。

normal.en: When repair is impossible, damages are money in its place.
normal.cn: 修不好时，赔偿金就是代替它的钱。

normal.en: If it costs something to fix, there was damage.
normal.cn: 如果修它要花钱，那就是有过损坏。

abstract.en: Picture a car roof covered in small round dents.
abstract.cn: 想象车顶布满一个个小圆坑。

abstract.en: Picture a cracked window that still keeps out rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇裂了却还能挡雨的窗。

abstract.en: Picture a folded paper with a sum written at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折起来的纸，末尾写着一个数额。

examples.en: The storm caused damage to the roof.
examples.cn: 暴风雨给屋顶造成了损坏。

examples.en: The hail damaged every car on the street.
examples.cn: 冰雹砸坏了街上每一辆车。

examples.en: The court ordered him to pay damages.
examples.cn: 法院命令他支付赔偿金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 damage 记成「打折」：东西被打折了，就是受了损；修不好，就用钱来赔。

root: 源自拉丁语 damnum（损失、代价），经古法语 damage 进入英语；本义是让人遭受损失，先指财物的损伤，后指法律上为弥补损失而支付的赔偿金。

sensesIntro.en: From the harm a blow leaves, to the act of harming, to the money that stands in for what was lost.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一击留下的损伤，到使人受损的动作，再到代替损失的那笔钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard blow landing on a surface and leaving a mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次重击落在表面上，留下痕迹。

branches.en: The noun names the harm itself.
branches.cn: 名词指伤害本身。

branches.en: The verb names the act that produces it.
branches.cn: 动词指造成它的那个动作。

branches.en: The plural turns the harm into a sum of money.
branches.cn: 复数把伤害变成一笔钱。

branches.en: The harm and the harming are two sides of one event.
branches.cn: 损伤与造成损伤，是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: What cannot be repaired is paid for instead.
branches.cn: 修不好的部分，就用钱来抵。

intro.en: Damage belongs to the Latin damnum family, where loss turns into harm and into money paid.
intro.cn: damage 属于拉丁语 damnum 这一族，「损失」在这里变成伤害与赔款。

latinIntro.en: The Latin damnum, loss, and damnare, to condemn, stand behind this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 damnum（损失）与 damnare（宣判）是这一族词的根。

items.example: The damage was easy to see.

items.exampleCN: 破损的箱子被退了回来。

items.example: They damned the plan as foolish.
items.exampleCN: 他们谴责这个计划愚蠢。

items.example: The old tale warned of damnation.
items.exampleCN: 那个古老的故事警告人会有永罚。

items.example: He spoke damagingly of his rival.
items.exampleCN: 他说了有害于对手的话。
水灾损失导致道路封闭。

definition_en: to move the body in rhythm with music
core_image: 一对人在木地板上随音乐移步、旋转
scene: 音乐一响，她就拉着同伴在院子里转起圈来。They began to dance as soon as the music started.
sceneCN: 这里 dance 指「跳舞」（第 1 个义项：随音乐移动身体）；句意是音乐一响他们就开始跳。

senses.title: Move the body to music
senses.definition: to move the feet and body in time with music
senses.definitionCN: 让脚步和身体跟上音乐的节拍
senses.example: They began to dance as soon as the music started.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐一响，他们就开始跳。
senses.why: The body answers a beat before the mind finds a word for it.
senses.whyCN: 身体先对节拍作出回应，脑子才找到词。

senses.title: A named set of steps
senses.definition: a particular style or fixed sequence of movements
senses.definitionCN: 某一种风格或一套固定的动作
senses.example: The drum dance has been passed down for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这支鼓舞已经传了几百年。
senses.why: Once the steps are fixed, they can be taught and handed on.
senses.whyCN: 步子一旦固定下来，就能教给别人、传下去。

senses.title: An evening of dancing
senses.definition: a social event at which people dance
senses.definitionCN: 人们聚在一起跳舞的社交活动
senses.example: They met at a college dance in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们是在春天的一场大学舞会上认识的。
senses.why: When strangers share a floor, the dancing becomes a meeting place.
senses.whyCN: 陌生人共处一块地板，跳舞就成了相遇的地方。

intro.en: Dance came through Old French dancier, a word of uncertain origin that may go back to Frankish.
intro.cn: dance 经古法语 dancier 进入英语，来源不确定，可能上溯到法兰克语。

items.en: A Germanic root may have meant to stretch or draw the limbs.
items.cn: 一个日耳曼词根可能表示伸展或拉动四肢。

items.en: Dancier covered both the moving and the meeting that went with it.
items.cn: dancier 既指动作，也指随之而来的聚会。

items.en: Dance entered English and was used for any rhythmic movement.
items.cn: dance 进入英语，泛指一切有节奏的动作。

items.en: The noun named the art itself, not only the act.
items.cn: 名词开始指这门艺术本身，而不只是动作。

items.en: Dance floor, dance hall, and dance music fixed the word in daily life.
items.cn: dance floor、dance hall 和 dance music 把这个词安进了日常生活。

note.en: The look-alike group rings the same final sound, and the meaning group names other kinds of bodily motion.
note.cn: 形近组收着同一个尾音，近义组则列出其他身体动作。

entries.definition: to walk with high, springing steps
to look at something quickly
a long spear used by a rider
to move slowly from side to side
to turn round and round very fast
to lift a foot and put it down again

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin where foot meets beat and end where strangers meet on a shared floor.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从脚踩上节拍开始，落到陌生人共处一块地板的相遇。

normal.en: A dance begins where the music and the foot agree.
normal.cn: 音乐与脚一合拍，舞就开始了。

normal.en: Learn the steps and the floor stops being an enemy.
normal.cn: 学会了步子，地板就不再是敌人。

normal.en: The dancer forgets the counting once the body remembers.
normal.cn: 身体一旦记住，舞者就忘了数拍子。

normal.en: Every village has a dance that belongs to its own soil.
normal.cn: 每个村子都有一支属于自己土地的舞。

normal.en: A dance is a conversation held without words.
normal.cn: 一支舞是一场不用词的交谈。

abstract.en: Picture a hall where every pair turns at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一个大厅，每一对人在同一刻转身。

abstract.en: Picture a drum setting the pace for a line of dancers.
abstract.cn: 想象一面鼓为一排舞者定下节奏。

abstract.en: Picture two strangers meeting in the middle of a song.
abstract.cn: 想象两个陌生人在一首歌中间相遇。

examples.en: They began to dance as soon as the music started.
examples.cn: 音乐一响，他们就开始跳。

examples.en: The drum dance filled the street with noise and colour.
examples.cn: 鼓舞让整条街热闹又鲜艳。

examples.en: She met her husband at a college dance.
examples.cn: 她是在一场大学舞会上遇见她丈夫的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dance 记成「蹬地」：d 是脚尖，ance 是绕圈，脚尖一蹬地，人就在音乐里转起来。

root: 经古法语 dancier 进入英语，更早的来源可能是法兰克语中表示伸展四肢的词根；十三世纪起指有节奏的身体动作，十六世纪起又指舞蹈这门艺术与跳舞的场合。

sensesIntro.en: From a body answering a beat, to a fixed set of steps, to a room full of people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身体回应节拍，到一套固定的步子，再到满屋子的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people turning on a wooden floor as the music plays.
core.cn: 核心意象：音乐响起，两个人在木地板上转身。

branches.en: The first sense is the body simply obeying the beat.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是身体单纯地服从节拍。

branches.en: Repeated motion hardens into a form that can be taught.
branches.cn: 重复的动作凝固成可以传授的形式。

branches.en: The form gathers people into one place for an evening.
branches.cn: 这种形式把人聚到一处，度过一个晚上。

branches.en: The act and the party share the same floor and the same music.
branches.cn: 动作和聚会共享同一块地板、同一段音乐。

branches.en: A named dance is what a party promises before anyone arrives.
branches.cn: 有了名字的舞，是舞会在人到来之前给出的承诺。

intro.en: Dance grows into the person who dances, the activity itself, and a cluster of fixed compounds.
intro.cn: dance 长出跳舞的人、这项活动本身，还有一串固定搭配。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved; the line runs through Old French back to a Germanic source.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不涉及拉丁词根，它经古法语上溯到一个日耳曼来源。

items.meaning: the activity of moving to music

items.exampleCN: 乐队演奏了适合跳舞的曲子。

items.example: The dance floor was full by nine.

items.meaning: a large room used for dancing
items.example: The old dance hall closed last year.
items.exampleCN: 那家老舞厅去年关门了。

items.meaning: a traditional dance of a region
items.example: The children learned a folk dance.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们学了一支民间舞。

items.meaning: a band that plays for dancing
items.example: A dance band played all evening.
items.exampleCN: 一支伴舞乐队演奏了一整晚。

definition_en: the possibility that someone or something will be harmed
core_image: 悬崖边没有护栏的一小段山路
scene: 山路拐弯处没有护栏，脚下就是深谷。The danger was clear to everyone in the car.
sceneCN: 这里 danger 指「危险」（第 1 个义项：可能造成伤害的处境）；句意是车里每个人都明白那有多险。

senses.title: The chance of being harmed
senses.definition: the state in which harm may come to someone
senses.definitionCN: 伤害可能落到某人身上的处境
senses.example: The danger was clear to everyone in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 车里每个人都明白那有多险。
senses.why: Danger is not the harm itself but the open door through which it may come.
senses.whyCN: 危险不是伤害本身，而是伤害可能进来的那扇门。

senses.title: A person or thing that threatens
senses.definition: someone or something that may cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害的人或事物
senses.example: Loose rocks are the main danger on this path.
senses.exampleCN: 松动的石块是这条路上最大的危险。
senses.why: We give the name of the feeling to the thing that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 我们把那种感受的名字，直接给了引起它的事物。

intro.en: Danger came from Old French dangier, which first meant the power a lord held over others.
intro.cn: danger 来自古法语 dangier，最初指领主对他人握有的权力。

items.en: Dominus meant a master with power over a household.
items.cn: dominus 指对一家之主握有权力的主人。

items.en: Dominarium named the range of that power.
items.cn: dominarium 指这种权力所能覆盖的范围。

items.en: Dangier shifted to the harm a powerful person could do.
items.cn: dangier 转而指有权者能造成的伤害。

items.en: Danger entered English as the state of being under someone's power.
items.cn: danger 进入英语时，指处在他人权力之下的状态。

items.en: The word lost its lord and kept only the risk of harm.
items.cn: 这个词丢掉了领主，只留下受伤害的风险。

note.en: The look-alike group plays on the -anger or -angle ending, and the meaning group ranks kinds of threat.
note.cn: 形近组玩的是 -anger 或 -angle 的结尾，近义组则排列不同程度的威胁。

entries.definition: a person who dances
to hang and swing loosely
a box that holds food for animals
the chance that something bad will happen
a source of danger in a place or activity
entries.definitionCN: 某地或某活动中危险的来源

entries.definition: a warning or sign of coming harm
entries.definitionCN: 伤害将至的警告或征兆

normalIntro.en: These hooks start at a cliff edge without a rail and end with a warning spoken aloud.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从没有护栏的崖边开始，落到一句说出口的警告。

normal.en: Danger is what the body notices before the mind explains it.
normal.cn: 危险是身体先察觉、脑子后解释的东西。

normal.en: A missing rail says more about danger than any sign.
normal.cn: 少了一段护栏，比任何标牌都更能说明危险。

normal.en: The word once meant a lord's power to hurt.
normal.cn: 这个词从前指领主伤人的权力。

normal.en: Shared danger makes strangers speak to each other.
normal.cn: 共同的危险让陌生人开口说话。

normal.en: Name the danger clearly and half of it is already handled.
normal.cn: 把危险说清楚，就已经应付了一半。

abstract.en: Picture a thin path with a valley on one side.
abstract.cn: 想象一条窄路，一边就是山谷。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held up to stop the group.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起来，让一行人停下。

abstract.en: Picture a dark shape moving where the light ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一个黑影在光线尽头移动。

examples.en: The danger was clear to everyone in the car.
examples.cn: 车里每个人都明白那有多险。

examples.en: The children were in danger near the fast river.
examples.cn: 孩子们在湍急的河边身处危险。

examples.en: He warned us of the dangers of smoking.
examples.cn: 他告诫我们吸烟的种种危害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 danger 记成「挡着」：danger 读起来像「挡着」，挡不住就有危险，所以要提前挡住。

root: 源自拉丁语 dominus（主人）及其派生 dominarium（权力范围），经古法语 dangier 进入英语，本义是「他人握有的权力」，中古英语里指受制于人的处境，十六世纪后专指受伤害的风险。

sensesIntro.en: From the state of being exposed to harm, to the very thing that threatens.
sensesIntro.cn: 从暴露在伤害之下的处境，到那个造成威胁的东西本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow path at a cliff edge with no rail.
core.cn: 核心意象：崖边一条没有护栏的窄路。

branches.en: The first sense is a condition, not an object: harm is possible.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一种处境，而不是东西：伤害有可能发生。

branches.en: The second sense points at the loose rock or the careless driver.
branches.cn: 第二个义项指向那块松石或那个粗心的司机。

branches.en: Condition and cause borrow the same word because one leads to the other.
branches.cn: 处境与原因共用一个词，因为前者由后者引来。

branches.en: Both senses sit inside the older idea of power over someone.
branches.cn: 两个义项都装在更早那个「对他人握有权力」的观念里。

branches.en: Remove the thing and the condition disappears with it.
branches.cn: 把那个东西拿走，处境也随之消失。

intro.en: Danger has grown a family of adjectives, adverbs, and verbs that all point back to risk.
intro.cn: danger 长出了一族形容词、副词和动词，全都指回风险。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is dominus, a master, whose power gave the word its first meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 dominus（主人），正是主人的权力给了这个词最初的含义。

items.example: That road is dangerous at night.

items.meaning: in a way that may cause harm

items.example: The dam could endanger the village.
The bird is an endangered species.

items.meaning: an area where harm is likely
items.example: They moved people out of the danger zone.
items.exampleCN: 他们把人们撤出危险区。

items.example: The crew asked for danger money.
items.exampleCN: 机组人员要求危险津贴。

items.meaning: a sign that harm is near
items.example: The red light is a danger signal.

latinEntries.example: Dominus gave the word its early sense of power.
latinEntries.exampleCN: dominus 给了这个词早年的权力之义。

definition_en: likely to hurt someone or cause damage
core_image: 一块松动的石头悬在头顶，随时可能落下
scene: 头顶那块石头看起来随时会掉下来。The cliff path looked dangerous in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 dangerous 指「危险的」（第 1 个义项：容易造成伤害的）；句意是雨天那条崖边小路看着很险。

senses.title: Likely to cause harm
senses.definition: able or likely to hurt a person or damage something
senses.definitionCN: 能够或很可能伤人或损坏东西的
senses.example: The cliff path looked dangerous in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨天那条崖边小路看着很险。
senses.why: The adjective points at the thing, not the feeling it gives us.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词指向事物本身，而不是它给我们的感受。

senses.title: Full of risk to health
senses.definition: harmful to health or safety over time
senses.definitionCN: 长期来看对健康或安全有害的
senses.example: Smoking is dangerous to health at any age.
senses.exampleCN: 任何年龄吸烟都危害健康。
senses.why: Harm does not need to be sudden to deserve the name.
senses.whyCN: 伤害不必突然发生，也配得上这个称呼。

intro.en: Dangerous is danger plus the Latin suffix -ous, meaning full of or having the quality of.
intro.cn: dangerous 由 danger 加拉丁后缀 -ous 构成，意思是「充满……的」或「具有……性质的」。

items.en: The suffix -osus meant full of a quality.
items.cn: 后缀 -osus 表示充满某种性质。

items.en: Old French used -ous forms for things full of a trait.
items.cn: 古法语用 -ous 形式形容充满某种特点的事物。

items.en: Dangerous appeared, meaning full of the power to harm.
items.cn: dangerous 出现，意为充满伤人的力量。

items.en: The word widened from people to roads, weather, and habits.
items.cn: 这个词从人扩展到道路、天气和习惯。

items.en: Dangerous now labels anything that may do harm at any speed.
items.cn: 如今凡是可能造成伤害的东西，无论快慢，都可用 dangerous 标记。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the danger stem, and the meaning group ranks how unsafe something is.
note.cn: 形近组共享 danger 这个词干，近义组则排列不安全的不同程度。

entries.definition: the chance that harm will come
in a way that may cause harm
entries.definitionCN: 以可能造成伤害的方式

entries.definition: at risk of dying out
involving the chance of loss or harm
entries.definitionCN: 带有损失或受伤可能的

entries.definition: not protected from harm
dangerous in a way that is hard to see

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a stone above the head and end with a habit that harms slowly.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从头顶的一块石头开始，落到一个慢慢伤人的习惯。

normal.en: A rock that has not fallen yet is still dangerous.
normal.cn: 还没落下的石头，依然是危险的。

normal.en: The word describes the road, not the fear in the driver.
normal.cn: 这个词形容路，而不是司机心里的怕。

normal.en: Slow harm is no less dangerous than fast harm.
normal.cn: 慢的伤害并不比快的伤害更安全。

normal.en: Anything called dangerous makes the body step back first.
normal.cn: 凡被称作危险的东西，身体都会先后退一步。

normal.en: Add -ous and the noun turns into a label for the thing itself.
normal.cn: 加上 -ous，名词就变成贴在事物本身上的标签。

abstract.en: Picture a warning sign half hidden by branches.
abstract.cn: 想象一块被树枝遮住一半的警示牌。

abstract.en: Picture a wire fence with one broken strand.
abstract.cn: 想象一道铁丝网，断了一股。

abstract.en: Picture a smiling dog that is not safe to touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一条看起来友好、却不能摸的狗。

examples.en: The cliff path looked dangerous in the rain.
examples.cn: 雨天那条崖边小路看着很险。

examples.en: It is dangerous to swim here alone.
examples.cn: 独自在这里游泳很危险。

examples.en: They moved the dangerous goods to a locked room.
examples.cn: 他们把危险品搬到一间上锁的屋子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dangerous 记成「危险ous」：danger 是危险，-ous 是「满满的」，合起来就是满是危险。

root: 由 danger（危险）加拉丁后缀 -ous（充满……的）构成，十四世纪进入英语，本指「满怀伤人力量的」；十七世纪起从人扩展到道路、天气与习惯，成为泛指一切可能致害之物的形容词。

sensesIntro.en: From a thing that can hurt you now, to a habit that hurts you slowly.
sensesIntro.cn: 从立刻能伤到你的东西，到慢慢伤你的习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a loose stone hanging above a narrow path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块松石悬在窄路上方。

branches.en: The first sense points at an object or place that can wound.
branches.cn: 第一个义项指向能够致伤的东西或地点。

branches.en: The second sense stretches the same label over years of small harm.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把同一个标签拉长到多年的细小伤害上。

branches.en: Both senses judge the source, not the person who meets it.
branches.cn: 两个义项判断的都是源头，而不是遇上它的人。

branches.en: A habit can be as dangerous as a falling rock.
branches.cn: 一个习惯可以和落石一样危险。

branches.en: The word always asks the same question: what could this do to me?
branches.cn: 这个词总在问同一个问题：它可能把我怎样？

intro.en: Dangerous is the adjective branch of the danger family, with the suffix -ous doing all the work.
intro.cn: dangerous 是 danger 家族的形容词分支，工作全由后缀 -ous 完成。

latinIntro.en: The suffix comes from Latin -osus, full of, added to a word that itself goes back to dominus.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀来自拉丁语 -osus（充满），加在一个本身可上溯到 dominus 的词上。

items.example: The road is dangerous after dark.
They measured the dangerousness of the chemical.
items.exampleCN: 他们评估了这种化学品的危险性。

items.example: The fire endangered the whole street.

items.exampleCN: 这座公园保护濒危动物。

items.meaning: driving in a way that risks harm
items.example: He was fined for dangerous driving.

definition_en: to be brave enough to do something difficult or risky
core_image: 站在跳水台边缘，脚尖探出去又收回来
scene: 他站在跳板尽头，深吸一口气才迈出去。No one dared to jump from the high board.
sceneCN: 这里 dare 指「敢」（第 1 个义项：有勇气去做）；句意是没人敢从那块高板上跳下去。

senses.title: Be brave enough to act
senses.definition: to have enough courage to do something you fear
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的勇气去做自己害怕的事
senses.example: No one dared to jump from the high board.
senses.exampleCN: 没人敢从那块高板上跳下去。
senses.why: The word measures courage against a fear that is already present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是在已经存在的恐惧面前，量一量勇气够不够。

senses.title: Challenge someone to try
senses.definition: to urge someone to do something risky by calling them afraid
senses.definitionCN: 用「你怕了」来挑动别人去做有风险的事
senses.example: They dared him to sing in front of the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他们激他在全班面前唱歌。
senses.why: To dare another is to hand your own courage over as a test.
senses.whyCN: 去激别人，就是把自己的勇气当作考题递过去。

intro.en: Dare goes back to Old English durran, an old verb that has kept its shape for a thousand years.
intro.cn: dare 可上溯到古英语 durran，这个古老动词的形状一千年几乎没变。

items.en: Durran meant to have courage for something feared.
items.cn: durran 意为对害怕之事仍有勇气。

items.en: The past tense dorste kept an older pattern of vowel change.
items.cn: 过去式 dorste 保留了更古老的元音变化规律。

items.en: The verb split into a full verb and a helper in questions and denials.
items.cn: 这个动词分成两类：实义动词，以及疑问和否定里的助动词。

items.en: The sense of challenging another person became common.
items.cn: 「挑动别人」的用法变得常见。

items.en: Dare survives mainly in set phrases and in the speech of the brave.
items.cn: 如今 dare 主要活在固定短语和勇敢者的嘴里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the long vowel and final r, and the meaning group names ways of facing risk.
note.cn: 形近组共享长元音和词尾 r，近义组则列出面对风险的不同方式。

entries.definition: loved or costing a lot
to move quickly and suddenly
not covered by anything
to go somewhere or do something risky
to put something valuable in danger
to face something fearful on purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a foot at the edge of a board and end with a voice saying try it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从跳板边缘的一只脚开始，落到一句「你试试」的声音。

normal.en: To dare is to move while the fear stays where it is.
normal.cn: 敢，就是恐惧原地不动，人却往前走了。

normal.en: The board is only high because the ground is far below.
normal.cn: 跳板之所以高，只因为地面在很远的下方。

normal.en: A dare from a friend is a test wrapped in a joke.
normal.cn: 朋友的一句激将，是用玩笑包着的考试。

normal.en: Dare not is the shortest way to say I am afraid.
normal.cn: dare not 是说出「我怕」最短的方式。

normal.en: Courage is measured by what it costs, not by the noise it makes.
normal.cn: 勇气看代价，不看响声。

abstract.en: Picture a toe testing the cold air beyond the board.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚趾试探跳板外的冷空气。

abstract.en: Picture a child pushed forward by a circle of friends.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子被一圈朋友推到前面。

abstract.en: Picture the second after the jump, when there is no way back.
abstract.cn: 想象跳下之后的第二秒，已无路可退。

examples.en: No one dared to jump from the high board.
examples.cn: 没人敢从那块高板上跳下去。

examples.en: She did not dare look back at the door.
examples.cn: 她不敢回头看那扇门。

examples.en: He dared his brother to eat the hot pepper.
examples.cn: 他激他弟弟去吃那根辣椒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dare 记成「往前一跺」：d 是脚，are 是「是」，脚一跺说「我敢」，就是 dare。

root: 源自古英语 durran（敢），属日耳曼语系古老的过去—现在动词，过去式 dorste 保留元音变化；中古英语时分成实义动词与疑问否定中的助动词，十六世纪又发展出「激将」之义。

sensesIntro.en: From a person finding courage inside, to a person handing a test to someone else.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个人在内心找到勇气，到把一场考试递到别人手里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot at the edge of a diving board.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚踩在跳板边缘。

branches.en: The first sense is the inward push that beats the fear.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是压过恐惧的那股内在推力。

branches.en: The second sense moves that push into the mouth of another person.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把那股推力放进另一个人的嘴里。

branches.en: Both senses test courage, one on yourself and one on a friend.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在考验勇气，一个考自己，一个考朋友。

branches.en: A challenge only works if the other person already wants to be brave.
branches.cn: 激将之所以有效，是因为对方本来就想做个勇敢的人。

branches.en: The same word covers the jump and the voice that orders it.
branches.cn: 同一个词既管那一跳，也管命令人跳的那把声音。

intro.en: Dare is a short, old family: the verb, its noun of courage, and a few tightly fixed phrases.
intro.cn: dare 这一族又短又老：一个动词、一个表勇气的名词，还有几个扣得很紧的短语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin here; dare is a native Germanic verb that has stayed close to its Old English form.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语；dare 是本族日耳曼动词，一直保留着接近古英语的形态。

items.example: Few dare to ask him directly.

items.meaning: bold and willing to take risks

items.example: She dressed daringly for the party.
items.exampleCN: 她为聚会打扮得很大胆。

items.meaning: a person who takes wild risks
items.example: The daredevil rode across the gap.
items.exampleCN: 那个鲁莽的人骑车越过了缺口。

items.example: I dare not tell her the truth.
How dare you speak to me like that!
items.exampleCN: 你怎么敢那样跟我说话！

items.meaning: a stronger challenge to do something
items.example: He gave his friend a double dare.
items.exampleCN: 他给朋友下了双倍的激将。

definition_en: having little or no light, or being deep in colour
core_image: 关灯后屋里只剩窗外一点微光
scene: 停电以后，走廊里伸手不见五指。The stairwell was dark and quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 dark 指「黑暗的」（第 1 个义项：缺少光线的）；句意是楼梯间又黑又静。

collocations.zh: 黑马；出人意料的获胜者

senses.title: With little or no light
senses.definition: receiving too little light to see clearly
senses.definitionCN: 光线太少，看不清东西
senses.example: The stairwell was dark and quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 楼梯间又黑又静。
senses.why: Dark is not a thing but a lack, and the eye feels the lack at once.
senses.whyCN: 黑暗不是东西，而是一种缺失，眼睛立刻就能感到。

senses.title: Deep in colour
senses.definition: closer to black than to white in shade
senses.definitionCN: 在色彩上更接近黑而不是白
senses.example: She wore a dark green coat to the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一件深绿色外套去参加葬礼。
senses.why: A deep colour swallows light the way a dark room does.
senses.whyCN: 深色吞掉光，和一间黑屋子吞掉光是一个道理。

senses.title: Hidden or gloomy
senses.definition: kept secret, or suggesting something unhappy
senses.definitionCN: 被保密的，或暗示着不快的
senses.example: There is a dark side to that cheerful story.
senses.exampleCN: 那个欢快的故事还有阴暗的一面。
senses.why: We hide things where the light cannot reach, and the same word follows them.
senses.whyCN: 我们把东西藏在光照不到的地方，同一个词也就跟了过去。

intro.en: Dark is an Old English word, deorc, with relatives across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: dark 是古英语词 deorc，在日耳曼语各语言里都有亲戚。

items.en: Deorc described a place without light and a mood without joy.
items.cn: deorc 既形容没有光的地方，也形容没有喜悦的心境。

items.en: A related Norse word kept the same sense of gloom.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语里的相关词保留了同样的阴郁之义。

items.en: Dark settled into its modern spelling and its two senses of light and colour.
items.cn: dark 固定为今天的拼法，并分出光线与颜色两种意思。

items.en: Dark horse appeared in racing before it named any surprise winner.
items.cn: dark horse 先出现在赛马中，后来才指任何出人意料的赢家。

items.en: In the dark now means kept from knowledge as well as from light.
items.cn: 如今 in the dark 既指身处黑暗，也指被人瞒着。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the d- opening and short vowel, and the meaning group moves from dim to joyless.
note.cn: 形近组共享 d 开头和短元音，近义组则从昏暗走到阴沉。

entries.definition: to be brave enough to do something
to move quickly and suddenly
unpleasantly damp and cold
entries.definitionCN: 阴冷潮湿得让人不舒服的

entries.definition: not bright, but still able to be seen
dark in a way that makes people sad
full of shadow and hard to see

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a switch turned off and end with a secret kept in the dark.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从按下开关那一刻开始，落到被藏在暗处的秘密。

normal.en: Dark is the shape a room takes when the light leaves.
normal.cn: 黑暗是光走后房间留下的形状。

normal.en: The eyes grow used to dark before the mind does.
normal.cn: 眼睛比心更早习惯黑暗。

normal.en: A dark colour holds the light instead of giving it back.
normal.cn: 深色把光留下，而不是还回去。

normal.en: What is kept in the dark is usually kept on purpose.
normal.cn: 被留在暗处的事，通常是故意留的。

normal.en: One small lamp changes the whole word.
normal.cn: 一盏小灯就能改变整个词的分量。

abstract.en: Picture a hand feeling along a wall for the switch.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手沿墙摸找开关。

abstract.en: Picture the last red line of a sunset going out.
abstract.cn: 想象落日最后一道红线熄灭。

abstract.en: Picture a face half in shadow at the end of a table.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌尽头一张半在阴影里的脸。

examples.en: The stairwell was dark and quiet.
examples.cn: 楼梯间又黑又静。

examples.en: She painted the door a dark red.
examples.cn: 她把门漆成了深红色。

examples.en: They walked home before dark.
examples.cn: 他们天黑前走回了家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dark 记成「打黑」：读音像「打黑」，一关灯就把屋子打进黑暗里。

root: 源自古英语 deorc（暗的、阴郁的），与古诺尔斯语等日耳曼语言中的相关词同源；中古英语固定为今天的拼法，并由「缺光」引申出「颜色深」与「隐秘、阴郁」两层意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a room without light, to a colour close to black, to a thing kept hidden.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有光的房间，到接近黑色的颜色，再到被藏起来的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room after the switch is turned off.
core.cn: 核心意象：开关按下之后的房间。

branches.en: The first sense is simply the absence of enough light.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是光线不够。

branches.en: The second transfers that absence to colour: black is light gone.
branches.cn: 第二个把这种缺失移到颜色上：黑就是光不见了。

branches.en: The third transfers it again, to knowledge and to mood.
branches.cn: 第三个再移一次，移到知识和心境上。

branches.en: Being in the dark about news is the same picture as being in a dark room.
branches.cn: 对消息一无所知，和待在一间黑屋子里是同一幅画。

branches.en: A dark colour and a dark secret both keep something out of sight.
branches.cn: 深色和阴暗的秘密，都把什么东西挡在视线之外。

intro.en: Dark has grown a compact family of verbs, nouns, and set phrases built on the same idea of lost light.
intro.cn: dark 长出一小族动词、名词和固定短语，都建立在「光不见了」这个意思上。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root stands behind dark; it is a native Germanic word from Old English deorc.
latinIntro.cn: dark 背后没有拉丁词根，它是古英语 deorc 传下来的本族日耳曼词。

items.meaning: in a gloomy or secret way
items.example: He spoke darkly of the future.

items.meaning: a room used for developing photographs
items.example: The photos dried in the darkroom.
She was the dark horse of the race.
He wore a dark blue shirt.

definition_en: the state of having no light, or the time when night has come
core_image: 没有月亮也没有灯的深夜
scene: 屋里没有一点光，只能听见自己的呼吸。The darkness pressed in from every side.
sceneCN: 这里 darkness 指「黑暗」（第 1 个义项：没有光的状态）；句意是黑暗从四面压过来。

senses.title: The absence of light
senses.definition: the condition in which there is no light to see by
senses.definitionCN: 没有可供视物的光线的状态
senses.example: The darkness pressed in from every side.
senses.exampleCN: 黑暗从四面压过来。
senses.why: It names a condition rather than a thing, which is why it has no plural.
senses.whyCN: 它命名的是一种状态而不是东西，所以没有复数。

senses.title: Night itself
senses.definition: the period or presence of night, when the world is unlit
senses.definitionCN: 夜晚到来、世界没有光的时候
senses.example: They set out under cover of darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 他们借着夜色出发。
senses.why: Night is darkness given a time and a name.
senses.whyCN: 夜，就是被安上时间和名字的黑暗。

senses.title: Evil or ignorance
senses.definition: a state of evil, or of being kept from the truth
senses.definitionCN: 邪恶的状态，或被人蒙住真相的状态
senses.example: The story is about light struggling with darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事讲的是光明与黑暗的搏斗。
senses.why: The oldest metaphor we have puts knowledge in the light and evil in the dark.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的比喻把知识放在光里，把邪恶放在暗里。

intro.en: Darkness is dark plus the Old English noun ending -ness, which turns a quality into a state.
intro.cn: darkness 由 dark 加古英语名词后缀 -ness 构成，把一种性质变成一种状态。

items.en: The ending -nes made nouns out of adjectives.
items.cn: 后缀 -nes 把形容词变成名词。

items.en: Deorcnes named the state of having no light.
items.cn: deorcnes 指没有光的状态。

items.en: The spelling settled as darkness and the word entered the Bible.
items.cn: 拼法固定为 darkness，这个词也进入了圣经。

items.en: Writers began using darkness for ignorance and moral evil.
items.cn: 作家开始用 darkness 指无知与道德上的恶。

items.en: Darkness now covers everything from a power cut to a fallen kingdom.
items.cn: 如今 darkness 从停电一直能说到覆灭的王国。

note.en: The look-alike group is a row of -ness nouns, and the meaning group names other kinds of shadow.
note.cn: 形近组是一排 -ness 名词，近义组则列出其他形式的阴影。

entries.definition: having little or no light
the state of being slightly wet
the condition of being unable to hear
a dark and sad half light
entries.definitionCN: 又暗又让人难过的微光

entries.definition: the dark shape a body throws
the dark part of every day

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin where the sun has gone and end where the word turns into a moral.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从太阳落下去的地方开始，落到这个词变成一句道理的地方。

normal.en: Darkness is not empty; it is full of things you cannot see.
normal.cn: 黑暗并不空，它装满了你看不见的东西。

normal.en: Sound grows louder when darkness takes the eyes.
normal.cn: 黑暗夺走眼睛，声音就变大。

normal.en: The word has no plural because a lack cannot be counted.
normal.cn: 这个词没有复数，因为缺失无法计数。

normal.en: Every lamp is an argument against darkness.
normal.cn: 每一盏灯都是对黑暗的一次反驳。

normal.en: We call evil dark because we cannot see our way through it.
normal.cn: 我们把恶叫作黑暗，因为身处其中看不清路。

abstract.en: Picture a field with no moon and no houses.
abstract.cn: 想象一片没有月亮也没有房屋的田野。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held out and not finding the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸出去，却摸不到墙。

abstract.en: Picture a single candle carried into a large hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛被带进一个大厅。

examples.en: The darkness pressed in from every side.
examples.cn: 黑暗从四面压过来。

examples.en: The village sat in total darkness after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨后整个村子一片漆黑。

examples.en: He waited in the darkness for the bus.
examples.cn: 他在黑暗中等着公交车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 darkness 记成「打黑尼斯」：dark 是黑，-ness 是状态，合起来就是黑成一片的那种状态。

root: 由 dark 加古英语名词后缀 -ness（表状态）构成，古英语作 deorcnes；中古英语固定为 darkness 并大量出现于宗教文本，十七世纪起引申指无知与道德上的邪恶。

sensesIntro.en: From a room with no light, to the night outside, to the dark we speak of in the soul.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有光的房间，到屋外的夜，再到我们说到人心里的那片暗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a night with neither moon nor lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：既无月也无灯的夜。

branches.en: The first sense is a condition measured by what is missing.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一种靠「缺了什么」来衡量的状态。

branches.en: The second gives that condition a time and calls it night.
branches.cn: 第二个给这种状态安上时间，叫它夜。

branches.en: The third moves it inward, where not seeing becomes not knowing.
branches.cn: 第三个把它移进人心，看不见就成了不明白。

branches.en: A power cut and a winter night produce the same picture.
branches.cn: 停电和冬夜造出同一幅画面。

branches.en: Night is when danger feels close, and the metaphor grows from that.
branches.cn: 夜里危险显得近，这个比喻就是从那里长出来的。

intro.en: Darkness is the noun of state built on dark, and it shares its family with the verb darken.
intro.cn: darkness 是建立在 dark 上的状态名词，与动词 darken 同属一族。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -ness is Germanic, not Latin; the whole word is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -ness 是日耳曼语成分，不是拉丁语；整个词都是英语本族词。

items.meaning: the state of having no light
items.exampleCN: 黑暗持续了好几个小时。

items.example: It was too dark to read.
The sky darkened before the rain.
She smiled darkly and said nothing.
items.exampleCN: 她阴郁地笑了笑，什么也没说。

items.example: The cave was in pitch darkness.

items.meaning: darkness with no light at all

definition_en: a person dearly loved; an affectionate form of address
core_image: 被捧在心口的称呼：对至亲之人的一声疼爱
scene: 奶奶在厨房门边招手，桌上刚出炉的饼干还冒着热气。"Come here, darling, and taste the biscuits," she smiled.
sceneCN: 这里 darling 是「亲爱的」（第 1 个义项：对至亲之人的亲昵称呼）；句意是奶奶招呼心爱的孩子来尝饼干。

pos.zh: 亲爱的；可爱的；讨人喜欢的

derivatives.zh: 基础词「亲爱的」，darling 由它加后缀构成
由 dear 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「深切地；珍爱地」
由 dear 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「亲爱；珍贵」

senses.title: A dearly loved person, as an address
senses.definition: someone you love very much, used when speaking to them
senses.definitionCN: 深受你爱的人，用作对本人说话时的称呼
senses.example: Goodnight, darling, sleep well.
senses.exampleCN: 晚安，亲爱的，睡个好觉。
senses.why: The suffix -ling turns 'dear' into a person: the one who is dear.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ling 把「亲爱的」变成「亲爱的人」，即被疼爱的那个人。

senses.title: A general friendly address, not only between lovers
senses.definition: a friendly or polite way of addressing someone you may barely know, especially in British speech
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中对未必熟识的人的友好称呼，常出自店主、长辈之口
senses.example: "That's three pounds, darling," said the shopkeeper.
senses.exampleCN: 「一共三镑，亲爱的。」店主说道。
senses.why: Family warmth spills into public politeness; the affectionate word becomes a social habit.
senses.whyCN: 家庭的温情溢出到公共礼貌中，亲昵称呼成了社交习惯。

senses.title: A person or thing especially favoured by a group
senses.definition: someone who is the current favourite of the public, media, or a community
senses.definitionCN: 公众、媒体或某群体当下最宠爱的人或事物
senses.example: The young actress quickly became the darling of the critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻女演员很快成了评论界的宠儿。
senses.why: Being loved by one person generalises into being loved by everyone, hence 'favourite'.
senses.whyCN: 「被一个人疼爱」推广为「被众人宠爱」，于是有了「宠儿」义。

senses.title: Charming or delightful (adjective)
senses.titleCN: 可爱的；讨人喜欢的（形容词）
senses.definition: attractive in a charming, endearing way
senses.definitionCN: 以迷人、惹人疼爱的样子吸引人的
senses.example: What a darling little hat she is wearing!
senses.exampleCN: 她戴的这顶小帽子真可爱！
senses.why: The feeling one has for a loved person transfers to anything that charms the same way.
senses.whyCN: 对心爱之人的情感转移到同样惹人怜爱的物件上，称呼词便转作形容词。

intro.en: Darling is dear plus the Old English person suffix -ling, a purely Germanic formation.
intro.cn: darling 是 dear 加古英语人称后缀 -ling 构成，纯日耳曼构词。

items.en: The reconstructed root *dēuz- or *dairiz is not secure; 'dear' is generally linked to a root meaning precious or valued, related to Old Norse dýrr.
items.cn: 「dear」的重构词根一般与「珍贵、有价值」义相关，与古诺斯语 dýrr 同源，重构形式，具体来源存疑。

items.en: Old English dēore meant dear or precious, and the suffix -ling made person words such as deorling, already used for a loved one.
items.cn: 古英语 dēore 意为「亲爱的、珍贵的」；后缀 -ling 构成人称词，deorling 一形已用于指心爱之人。

items.en: Middle English dereling and darling spread as a term for a beloved person, in both romance and family contexts.
items.cn: 中古英语 dereling、darling 广泛用于指心爱之人，涵盖爱情与家庭语境。

items.en: Shakespeare's plays use darling both as address and as adjective; the 'favourite of a group' sense begins to appear.
items.cn: 莎士比亚剧作中 darling 已兼作称呼与形容词；「群体宠儿」义开始出现。

items.en: Modern British speech keeps it as a friendly address to strangers, while media language calls celebrities the darlings of a group.
items.cn: 现代英式口语保留了对陌生人的友好称呼用法，媒体语言则称名人为何种群体的 darling。

note.en: Darling sits in a family of -ling person words and a group of affectionate addresses; separate it from look-alike darning.
note.cn: darling 属于 -ling 人称后缀词族和亲昵称呼词群；注意与形近的 darning 区分。

entries.definition: the activity of mending holes in cloth
entries.definitionCN: 「织补」，与 darling 仅一字母之差，词源不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: British money of high quality, or excellent quality generally
entries.definitionCN: 「英镑；纯银；优质的」，同为 -ling 结尾的形近词，词义无关

entries.definition: a young duck
entries.definitionCN: 「小鸭」，共享 -ling 后缀（小或称谓义），可对照记忆

entries.definition: a person you love; an affectionate address
entries.definitionCN: 「甜心；爱人」，同为亲昵称呼，语感稍浪漫

entries.definition: American informal affectionate address
entries.definitionCN: 美式口语「亲爱的」，与 darling 第 1、2 义项对应

entries.definition: British informal, especially northern, for a dear person
entries.definitionCN: 英式（尤北部）口语「宝贝」，与 darling 第 2 义项相近

normalIntro.en: Break darling into dear + -ling and compare its address family.
normalIntro.cn: 把 darling 拆成 dear 加 -ling，再对照称呼词族记忆。

normal.en: dear + -ling = the person who is dear; the suffix makes a person word.
normal.cn: dear 加 -ling 即「亲爱的人」，后缀把形容词变成人称词。

normal.en: Compare duckling, nestling: -ling marks a small or cherished being.
normal.cn: 对比 duckling、nestling：-ling 表示幼小或被疼爱者。

normal.en: British shopkeepers say darling to anyone; it can be pure politeness.
normal.cn: 英国店主对谁都叫 darling，可以是纯粹的客套。

normal.en: Phrase: the darling of the media = the current favourite.
normal.cn: 短语 the darling of the media 即「媒体当前的宠儿」。

normal.en: As adjective it means charming: a darling little cottage.
normal.cn: 作形容词表「可爱」：a darling little cottage 一座可爱小屋。

abstract.en: Feel the word spoken close to the ear, softly and warmly.
abstract.cn: 感受这声称呼贴着耳边轻轻说出的温度。

abstract.en: Picture grandma holding warm biscuits out to a child.
abstract.cn: 想象奶奶把热饼干递向孩子的画面。

abstract.en: See a rising star surrounded by flashing cameras, everyone's favourite.
abstract.cn: 看一个新星被闪光灯包围，成为众人宠儿。

examples.en: She held her darling daughter close before the journey.
examples.cn: 旅行前她把心爱的女儿紧紧搂在怀里。

examples.en: "Come here, darling, and taste the biscuits," grandma smiled.
examples.cn: 「过来，宝贝，尝尝饼干。」奶奶笑着说。

examples.en: The novel made its young author the darling of the literary world.
examples.cn: 这部小说让年轻作者一夜成为文学界的宠儿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「达令」——旧译「达令」即「令（人怜爱）到达心里的人」；谐音仅助记，真实构词是 dear 加后缀 -ling。

root: 古英语 dēore（亲爱的、珍贵的；词根一般认为与「珍贵」义相关，重构形式，来源存疑）+ 人称后缀 -ling（表「属于某类的人或幼小者」）；纯日耳曼构词，与拉丁语无关。

sensesIntro.en: From the loved person by name, outward to friendly public address, upward to the public favourite, and sideways into an adjective of charm.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对心爱之人的称呼出发，外扩为对陌生人的客套称呼，上抬为公众宠儿，再侧转为「可爱」的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name spoken with tenderness to the one held closest
core.cn: 核心意象：对最亲近之人温柔唤出的那声称呼

branches.en: the loved one addressed directly
branches.cn: 对心爱之人的当面称呼

branches.en: friendly address beyond intimacy
branches.cn: 溢出亲密关系的友好称呼

branches.en: the favourite of media or a crowd
branches.cn: 媒体或群体的宠儿

branches.en: charming things called darling
branches.cn: 被称作 darling 的可爱事物

branches.en: affection felt and charm shown
branches.cn: 被疼爱的情感与讨喜的特质相通

intro.en: Darling combines the adjective dear with the person suffix -ling; its family shows how English names beloved and small beings.
intro.cn: darling 由形容词 dear 加人称后缀 -ling 构成；其词族展示英语如何为「被爱者、幼小者」命名。

latinIntro.en: Darling has no Latin ancestry; both dear and -ling are Germanic, so no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: darling 无拉丁语来源；dear 与 -ling 均为日耳曼成分，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.meaningCN: 亲爱的、珍贵的，darling 的词基

items.meaning: one connected with; a young one
items.meaningCN: 古英语后缀，构成「某类人」或「幼崽」
darling 的古英语前身，义为「心爱的人」

items.example: the twins are mother's little darlings
items.exampleCN: 双胞胎是妈妈的小宝贝。

items.meaningCN: 「织补」，形近词，词源与 darling 无关
深切地；由基础词 dear 派生

definition_en: a large set of information stored in a computer and arranged for quick searching
core_image: 一间排满文件柜、每格都贴着编号的房间
scene: 前台一输入名字，屏幕上立刻跳出档案。The database found her record in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 database 指「数据库」（第 1 个义项：有结构地存放数据的系统）；句意是数据库几秒内就找到了她的记录。

senses.title: An organized store of data
senses.definition: a large body of information arranged so that it can be searched quickly
senses.definitionCN: 按一定方式排列、便于快速检索的大量信息
senses.example: The database found her record in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库几秒内就找到了她的记录。
senses.why: The power lies not in the amount of data but in the order it is kept in.
senses.whyCN: 力量不在数据多少，而在它们被放得多有次序。

senses.title: The software that runs it
senses.definition: the program or system that stores and answers questions about such data
senses.definitionCN: 负责存放数据并回答查询的程序或系统
senses.example: The team installed a new database last month.
senses.exampleCN: 团队上个月装了新的数据库系统。
senses.why: We use one word for the store and for the machine that guards it.
senses.whyCN: 我们用一个词同时指这座仓库和看守它的机器。

intro.en: Database is a modern coinage joining data, the plural of Latin datum, to base, a foundation.
intro.cn: database 是现代的造词，把拉丁语 datum 的复数 data（数据）与 base（基础）拼在一起。

items.en: Datum meant something given, a fact handed over.
items.cn: datum 意为「被给出的东西」，即交出的事实。

items.en: Data entered English as the plural of datum.
items.cn: data 作为 datum 的复数进入英语。

items.en: Data bank named a store of facts kept for later use.
items.cn: data bank 指为日后使用而存放事实的库。

items.en: Database was coined for computer files that could be searched.
items.cn: database 被造出来，指可检索的计算机文件集合。

items.en: Database now covers everything from a phone list to a national registry.
items.cn: 如今 database 从电话簿一直指到国家登记系统。

note.en: The look-alike group breaks the compound into its parts, and the meaning group names other collections of records.
note.cn: 形近组把这个复合词拆成部件，近义组则列出其他形式的记录集合。

entries.definition: facts and figures collected for use
entries.definitionCN: 为使用而收集的事实与数字

entries.definition: the bottom or starting point of something
a large store of information
a store of old records kept for reference
entries.definitionCN: 为查考而保存旧记录的地方

entries.definition: an official list kept in order
a book of records kept in rows

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a wall of numbered drawers and end with an answer appearing in a second.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一面编号抽屉的墙开始，落到一秒内跳出来的答案。

normal.en: A database is a library where no book is out of place.
normal.cn: 数据库是一座没有一本书放错位置的图书馆。

normal.en: Order is the only thing that makes a million facts useful.
normal.cn: 让一百万条事实变得有用的，只有次序。

normal.en: The word joins what is given to the ground it stands on.
normal.cn: 这个词把「被给出的东西」接到了「它立足的地基」上。

normal.en: A question asked well is already half an answer.
normal.cn: 问得好的问题，已经是一半的答案。

normal.en: Every record is a person who once filled in a form.
normal.cn: 每条记录背后，都是一个曾经填过表的人。

abstract.en: Picture a long room of grey cabinets with small labels.
abstract.cn: 想象一间长屋子，摆满贴着小标签的灰色柜子。

abstract.en: Picture a cursor blinking beside an empty search box.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空搜索框旁闪烁的光标。

abstract.en: Picture one line of text rising to the top of a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一行字升到屏幕最上方。

examples.en: The database found her record in seconds.
examples.cn: 数据库几秒内就找到了她的记录。

examples.en: All the patient records are kept in one database.
examples.cn: 所有病人记录都存在同一个数据库里。

examples.en: They built a database of local plant names.
examples.cn: 他们建了一个本地植物名称的数据库。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 database 记成「数据基地」：data 是数据，base 是基地，数据存放的基地就是数据库。

root: 由 data（数据，拉丁语 datum「被给出之物」的复数）与 base（基础、基地）复合而成，二十世纪六十年代随计算机检索系统出现，指按结构存放、便于查询的大量信息。

sensesIntro.en: From the ordered store of facts, to the system that keeps answering for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从按序存放的事实，到替它回答问题的系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room of numbered drawers, each holding one kind of fact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间编了号的抽屉房，每格装着一种事实。

branches.en: The first sense is the store itself, judged by its order.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是仓库本身，以次序论高低。

branches.en: The second sense is the machine that reads and answers.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是负责读取和回答的机器。

branches.en: The store and the system are named together because neither works alone.
branches.cn: 仓库与系统合称，因为缺了谁都不成。

branches.en: A drawer never answers; the index does.
branches.cn: 抽屉从不回答，回答的是索引。

branches.en: The system is only as good as the order it inherited.
branches.cn: 系统的水平，取决于它继承下来的那套次序。

intro.en: Database is a compound, so its family is built by joining data and base to other words.
intro.cn: database 是个复合词，它的一族靠把 data 与 base 同别的词拼起来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is datum, something given; base is Greek in origin, a step or foundation.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁成分是 datum（被给出之物）；base 源自希腊语，意为台阶或基础。

items.example: The hospital keeps a databank of scans.
items.exampleCN: 医院存有一个扫描资料库。

items.meaning: software for storing and searching data
the work of keeping a database in order
a database reached through a network
items.example: The journal is in an online database.
items.exampleCN: 这份期刊在一个在线数据库里。

items.meaning: a person who looks after a database
items.example: Only the database administrator can change it.
items.exampleCN: 只有数据库管理员能改动它。

latinEntries.example: Datum is the singular behind data.
latinEntries.exampleCN: datum 是 data 背后的单数形式。

definition_en: a particular day of a month or year, or an arranged meeting
core_image: 日历上用红笔圈出的一个日子
scene: 她翻到日历上圈红的那一天，在旁边写下名字。He wrote the date at the top of the letter.
sceneCN: 这里 date 指「日期」（第 1 个义项：某一天的具体时间）；句意是他在信纸顶部写上了日期。

senses.title: A particular day
senses.definition: the exact day shown by a number, month, and year
senses.definitionCN: 用日、月、年标出的具体某一天
senses.example: He wrote the date at the top of the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他在信纸顶部写上了日期。
senses.why: A date makes one day stand out from all the others.
senses.whyCN: 日期让某一天从所有日子里站出来。

senses.title: A meeting with someone you like
senses.definition: an arrangement to meet a person you are fond of
senses.definitionCN: 与喜欢的人约定见面
senses.example: They had a date at the little cafe.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在那家小咖啡馆有个约会。
senses.why: The word for a fixed day became the word for a fixed meeting.
senses.whyCN: 表示定好日子的词，后来变成了表示定好见面的词。

senses.title: To have existed since
senses.definition: to show or have a starting point in past time
senses.definitionCN: 显示出或拥有某个过去的时间起点
senses.example: The church dates back to the twelfth century.
senses.exampleCN: 这座教堂可追溯到十二世纪。
senses.why: To date something is to pin it to a day on a long line.
senses.whyCN: 给某物定日期，就是把它钉在一条长线上的某一点。

intro.en: Date comes from Latin data, the word written at the head of a letter to say where and when it was given.
intro.cn: date 来自拉丁语 data，原是在信首注明该信于何时何地「交出」的字样。

items.en: Dare meant to give or hand over.
items.cn: dare 意为给出、交出。

items.en: Letters opened with data, given, followed by the place and day.
items.cn: 信件以 data（交出于）开头，后面写地点与日子。

items.en: French date named the day written on a document.
items.cn: 法语 date 指写在文书上的那一天。

items.en: Date entered English with the same documentary sense.
items.cn: date 以同样的文书含义进入英语。

items.en: The palm fruit had a different origin, named for a finger.
items.cn: 枣这一义项另有来源，因形似手指而得名。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ate shape, and the meaning group names other points and meetings in time.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ate 的词形，近义组则列出时间上的其他节点与相见。

entries.definition: facts collected for use
the power that decides what will happen
to be brave enough to do something
a period of twenty-four hours
entries.definitionCN: 二十四小时的一段时间

entries.definition: a fixed time arranged for a meeting
a plan that lists times for events
entries.definitionCN: 列出各项活动时间的计划表

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a day circled in red and end with a building that remembers its own beginning.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被红笔圈起的一天开始，落到一座记得自己起点的建筑。

normal.en: A date turns a plain day into a place you can point at.
normal.cn: 日期把平常的一天，变成你能指出来的一点。

normal.en: The word once sat at the top of a letter, saying this was given today.
normal.cn: 这个词从前坐在信头，说明此信今日交出。

normal.en: Out of date is only time doing its work.
normal.cn: 过时，不过是时间在做它的事。

normal.en: A first date is a whole day shrunk into one hour.
normal.cn: 初次约会，是一整天缩进一小时里。

normal.en: To date a ruin is to give it a birthday.
normal.cn: 给一处遗址定年代，就是给它一个生日。

abstract.en: Picture a red circle on a wall calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上日历里的一个红圈。

abstract.en: Picture two cups on a table and no clock in sight.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上有两只杯子，四下看不见钟。

abstract.en: Picture a stone wall with a carved year above the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一面石墙，门上方刻着年份。

examples.en: He wrote the date at the top of the letter.
examples.cn: 他在信纸顶部写上了日期。

examples.en: The church dates back to the twelfth century.
examples.cn: 这座教堂可追溯到十二世纪。

examples.en: They had a date at the little cafe.
examples.cn: 他们在那家小咖啡馆有个约会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 date 记成「待特」：特别的一天值得等，等到了就是约会，写下来就是日期。

root: 源自拉丁语 data（被交出之物，dare「给出」的过去分词），古时书信开头写 data 再加地点日期；经法语 date 于十四世纪进入英语，先指文书上的日子，后引申为约会与追溯年代。枣的义项另有希腊语来源，与日期无关。

sensesIntro.en: From one marked day, to a meeting fixed on that day, to the day a thing began.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被标记的一天，到定在那天的相见，再到某物开始的那一天。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single day circled in red on a calendar.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上被红笔圈起的一天。

branches.en: The first sense is the plain mark on the calendar.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是日历上那道朴素的记号。

branches.en: The second puts two people on that mark at the same hour.
branches.cn: 第二个把两个人放在那道记号的同一时刻上。

branches.en: The third sends the mark backwards along the years.
branches.cn: 第三个把这道记号沿着年份往回送。

branches.en: A date on paper and a date with a person both mean a fixed point for meeting.
branches.cn: 纸上的日期和与人的约会，都指一个定好的相遇点。

branches.en: To date an object is to write its day in the past.
branches.cn: 给一件东西定年代，就是把它那一天写到过去。

intro.en: Date forms a wide but shallow family, mostly adjectives made with -ed and -able.
intro.cn: date 的一族宽而浅，大多是用 -ed 和 -able 造出的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is dare, to give; data is what has been given.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 dare（给出），data 就是被给出的东西。

items.meaning: marked with a date, or out of fashion
items.example: The letter was dated May first.
items.exampleCN: 那封信注明是五月一日。

items.meaning: having no date written on it
items.example: An undated photo lay on the desk.
items.exampleCN: 桌上有一张未标日期的照片。

items.meaning: able to be given a date
items.example: The coin is datable to the third century.
items.exampleCN: 这枚钱币可定到三世纪。

items.example: She opened her datebook to June.
items.exampleCN: 她翻开记事日历到六月。

items.example: Keep the list up to date.
The map is out of date.
The custom dates back to the war.
items.exampleCN: 这个风俗可追溯到战争年代。

definition_en: a single piece of information used as a basis for reasoning
core_image: 实验记录本上单独的一行读数
scene: 笔记本上只写了一行读数，却是全部测量的起点。One datum was enough to change their conclusion.
sceneCN: 这里 datum 指「数据」（第 1 个义项：单条资料或数值）；句意是一个数据就足以改变他们的结论。

senses.title: One piece of information
senses.definition: a single fact or figure used as a basis for a conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 作为推理依据的单独一条事实或数值
senses.example: One datum was enough to change their conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 一个数据就足以改变他们的结论。
senses.why: The singular keeps its place even when most people say data for one thing.
senses.whyCN: 即使多数人用 data 指一条，单数形式仍守着它的位置。

senses.title: A fixed reference point
senses.definition: a fixed point from which heights or positions are measured
senses.definitionCN: 测量高度或位置时所依据的固定点
senses.example: All heights were taken from the same datum.
senses.exampleCN: 所有高度都从同一个基准点量起。
senses.why: Measuring needs one point that does not move.
senses.whyCN: 要测量，就得有一个不动的点。

intro.en: Datum is Latin for something given, the neuter form of the past participle of dare, to give.
intro.cn: datum 在拉丁语中意为「被给出之物」，是 dare（给出）过去分词的中性形式。

items.en: Dare meant to give, hand over, or grant.
items.cn: dare 意为给出、交出、授予。

items.en: Datum named a thing given, a starting point granted for argument.
items.cn: datum 指被给出之物，即论证时被授予的起点。

items.en: Surveyors used datum for the fixed point of a measurement.
items.cn: 测量师用 datum 指测量的固定基点。

items.en: Scientists took datum into the language of experiment.
items.cn: 科学家把 datum 带进实验的语言。

items.en: The plural data has largely taken over, leaving datum to careful writers.
items.cn: 复数 data 已在多数场合接管，datum 留给讲究用法的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dat- opening, and the meaning group names other single units of knowledge.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dat- 开头，近义组则列出其他单个知识单位。

entries.definition: facts collected for use
a particular day of the year
the case of the indirect object
entries.definitionCN: 表示间接宾语的语法格

entries.definition: something known to be true
a number that records an amount
a single number taken from a set of records
entries.definitionCN: 从一组记录中取出的单个数字

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one line in a notebook and end with a surveyor's fixed mark in the ground.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从笔记本上的一行字开始，落到测量员钉在地里的固定标记。

normal.en: One datum is a stone; data is the wall built from it.
normal.cn: 一个数据是一块石头，数据是一堵用石头砌成的墙。

normal.en: The word means given, because a fact is handed to you before you reason.
normal.cn: 这个词意为「被给出」，因为事实总在你推理之前就被递到手上。

normal.en: Keep the singular and you keep the habit of counting carefully.
normal.cn: 守住单数，就守住了仔细计数的习惯。

normal.en: Every measurement needs one point that refuses to move.
normal.cn: 每次测量都需要一个不肯移动的点。

normal.en: Datum is the word a careful engineer still writes in a report.
normal.cn: 严谨的工程师在报告里仍然会写 datum。

abstract.en: Picture a single number underlined twice in a lab book.
abstract.cn: 想象实验本上一个被划了两道线的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a brass pin set in concrete before any building starts.
abstract.cn: 想象动工之前，一枚铜钉被嵌进混凝土。

abstract.en: Picture one dot on a graph with nothing else drawn yet.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上只画了一个点，别的都还没有。

examples.en: One datum was enough to change their conclusion.
examples.cn: 一个数据就足以改变他们的结论。

examples.en: All heights were taken from the same datum.
examples.cn: 所有高度都从同一个基准点量起。

examples.en: Each datum in the table was checked twice.
examples.cn: 表格里的每一条数据都核对了两遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 datum 记成「得Ta」：得（dei）到一个答案，靠的就是这一条数据。

root: 拉丁语 datum 意为「被给出之物」，是 dare（给出）的过去分词中性形式，最初指论证前已被授予的起点；十七世纪进入英语测量术语，指固定基准点，十八世纪起成为实验与统计中单个事实或数值的名称。

sensesIntro.en: From one given fact, to the fixed point from which all measuring starts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被给出的一条事实，到一切测量所依据的那个定点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one underlined number in a notebook of measurements.
core.cn: 核心意象：测量笔记本里一个画了线的数字。

branches.en: The first sense is the smallest unit of evidence.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是证据的最小单位。

branches.en: The second turns the unit into a point in space.
branches.cn: 第二个把这个单位变成空间中的一个点。

branches.en: Both senses need something given before anything can be built.
branches.cn: 两个义项都要先有「被给出的东西」，才能开始搭建。

branches.en: A surveyor's mark is itself one datum among many.
branches.cn: 测量员的标记本身也是众多数据中的一条。

branches.en: The word keeps asking where the figure came from.
branches.cn: 这个词始终在问：这个数字是从哪里来的。

intro.en: Datum is the singular trunk from which data, database, and databank all branch.
intro.cn: datum 是主干单数，data、database 与 databank 都从它分枝出去。

latinIntro.en: The Latin participle datum, given, is the source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语分词 datum（被给出的）是整个词族的源头。

items.example: A single datum cannot prove the theory.
items.exampleCN: 一个数据无法证明这个理论。

items.example: The database holds ten years of records.
items.exampleCN: 这个数据库存着十年的记录。

items.example: The databank is open to researchers.

items.meaning: the fixed point of a survey
items.example: They set a datum point on the hill.
items.exampleCN: 他们在山上设了基准点。

items.meaning: the line drawn from that point
the surface used as a base

items.example: Each raw datum went into the file.
items.exampleCN: 每条原始数据都进了档案。

latinEntries.example: Dare is the verb behind datum.
latinEntries.exampleCN: dare 是 datum 背后的动词。

definition_en: a person's female child
core_image: 母亲蹲下来，替小女孩把围巾系好
scene: 门口，母亲蹲下来替女儿系好围巾。Their daughter waved from the school gate.
sceneCN: 这里 daughter 指「女儿」（第 1 个义项：父母所生的女孩）；句意是他们的女儿在校门口挥手。

senses.title: A female child of a parent
senses.definition: a girl or woman in relation to her mother or father
senses.definitionCN: 相对于母亲或父亲而言的女孩或女子
senses.example: Their daughter waved from the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的女儿在校门口挥手。
senses.why: English keeps a separate old word for the female child, not a form of son.
senses.whyCN: 英语为女性孩子留了一个单独的老词，而不是在 son 上变化。

senses.title: A woman shaped by a place
senses.definition: a woman seen as the product of a place, group, or period
senses.definitionCN: 被视为某地、某群体或某时代产物的女子
senses.example: She called herself a daughter of the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 她称自己是山的女儿。
senses.why: The family word becomes a metaphor whenever a source feels like a parent.
senses.whyCN: 只要一个源头像父母，家庭的词就会变成比喻。

intro.en: Daughter is one of the oldest words in English, with close relatives in almost every Indo-European language.
intro.cn: daughter 是英语中最古老的词之一，在几乎每种印欧语言里都有近亲。

items.en: A root for daughter survives in Greek and Sanskrit alike.
items.cn: 表示女儿的同一词根，在希腊语和梵语里都活着。

items.en: Dohtor named a female child in the family.
items.cn: dohtor 指家中的女性孩子。

items.en: Norse settlers brought a related form that reinforced the word.
items.cn: 诺尔斯移民带来相关词形，强化了这个词。

items.en: The spelling shifted to doughter before settling as daughter.
items.cn: 拼写先变为 doughter，后来才固定为 daughter。

items.en: Daughter now also names a woman as the child of a place or an age.
items.cn: 如今 daughter 也指某地或某时代的女儿。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -aughter or -octor ending, and the meaning group names other family roles.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -aughter 或 -octor 的结尾，近义组则列出其他家庭角色。

entries.definition: the sound of people laughing
the killing of many animals or people
a person trained to treat illness
a young person of either sex
a female child or young woman
the young of a person or animal

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a scarf being tied at the door and end with a woman naming the mountain she came from.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从门口系好的围巾开始，落到一个女子说出自己来自哪座山。

normal.en: The word is older than England itself.
normal.cn: 这个词比英格兰还要老。

normal.en: A daughter is a child who will one day be the one bending down.
normal.cn: 女儿是会有一天弯下腰的那个人。

normal.en: The word does not come from son; it has always stood on its own.
normal.cn: 这个词不是从 son 变来的，它一直自己站着。

normal.en: Call a river a parent and a city becomes its daughter.
normal.cn: 把一条河叫作母亲，一座城就成了它的女儿。

normal.en: Family words are the easiest to turn into metaphors.
normal.cn: 家庭的词，最容易变成比喻。

abstract.en: Picture small shoes lined up beside a larger pair.
abstract.cn: 想象一双小鞋挨着一双大鞋摆好。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a shoulder at a school gate.
abstract.cn: 想象校门口一只手搭在肩上。

abstract.en: Picture an old photograph of a girl who is now a grandmother.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧照片，照片里的女孩如今已是祖母。

examples.en: Their daughter waved from the school gate.
examples.cn: 他们的女儿在校门口挥手。

examples.en: She is the eldest daughter of three.
examples.cn: 三个孩子里她是长女。

examples.en: He walked his daughter to the bus stop.
examples.cn: 他送女儿走到公交站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 daughter 记成「多特」：家里多了一个特别的人，就是女儿。

root: 源自古英语 dohtor，属印欧语系最古老的亲属称谓之一，与希腊语、梵语中的同源词对应；中古英语拼写先作 doughter，后固定为 daughter，现代又引申指某地或某时代的女儿。

sensesIntro.en: From a girl in a family, to a woman who belongs to a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从家庭里的女孩，到属于某个地方的女子。
